title: Shafa‘ah, Mizan and the Sirat bridge
intro: Intercession, the scales, the Prophet’s pool and the bridge over Jahannam.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: The weighing that Day will be just: those whose good deeds are heavy will succeed, and those whose good deeds are light have lost themselves, because they rejected Allah’s signs. <small>(Qur’an, Al-A‘raf 7:8–9)</small>

The gathering of all people who ever lived will mark the start of the Day of Judgement – the day when people’s deeds are shown and Allah judges them. Every person must do good, but however much good a person does, they cannot earn Jannah by it alone: after the judgement the believers will enter Jannah by Allah’s mercy.

Shafa‘ah is the right of prophets, martyrs (shuhada), the friends of Allah and other chosen people to intercede for others on the Day of Judgement. The Qur’an will intercede for those who recited it and lived by it. Interceding means asking Allah to forgive those who deserve it, through those He gave this right. Shafa‘ah is only possible for those Allah allows. The prophets will intercede for their followers – Muhammad (SAW) for those of his ummah who followed his sunnah. Martyrs and other chosen people will intercede for their families.

The Mizan is the perfect scale of the Day of Judgement, on which people’s deeds will be weighed. It has two pans: good deeds go on one and bad deeds on the other. With the weighing, Allah’s perfect justice will be done, and no one will be wronged that Day.

learn.title: Heavy on the scales
learn.html: Some deeds are especially heavy on the Mizan. The Prophet (SAW) said: “Cleanliness is half of iman, and the words Alhamdulillah fill the Mizan.” (Muslim)

The Hawd is the pool of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW), fed from the river Kawthar, at the reckoning on the Day of Judgement. On that Day the Prophet (SAW) and the believers of his ummah will drink from it. He said: “My pool is as wide as a month’s journey. Its water is whiter than milk and its smell sweeter than musk; its cups are like the stars in the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again.” (Bukhari)

The Sirat is the bridge over Jahannam. Those rewarded with Jannah will cross it; for those punished with Jahannam it will be an obstacle. Allah tells us that every one of us will come to it; then He will save those who feared Him. (Qur’an, Maryam 19:71–72)

The Sirat is sharper than a sword, thinner than a hair and slippery – only those Allah keeps steady will stay upright. Some believers will cross it in the blink of an eye, some like lightning, some like the wind, some like birds, some like running horses, some hurrying – and the last will cross crawling.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: After crossing the Sirat, and after the believers settle their accounts with each other, they will be allowed to enter Jannah.
